findings.problem: status: String allows any string value including invalid transitions like 'sent' without validation, or garbage like 'banana', '', or 'SENT'; typestate review requires enum
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct BudgetWorkflow with status='banana' or transition directly to 'sent' without going through validated, making illegal states representable at compile time
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with `status: BudgetStatus` enum with explicit variants (Pending, Validated, Sent, Rejected); remove `is_validated` and `is_sent` booleans

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can be in impossible combinations (both false, both true, validated but not sent, sent but not validated, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: Business logic cannot guarantee that only validated budgets are sent; callers can set is_validated=true and is_sent=true simultaneously without ever passing validation, or set is_sent=true with status='pending'
findings.fix: Remove both booleans. Replace with a single BudgetStatus enum whose variants encode the full lifecycle state, e.g. `BudgetStatus::Pending`, `BudgetStatus::Validated`, `BudgetStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is optional lifecycle data stored as a separate field rather than owned by the variant that needs it; it can be None while is_sent=true, or Some while status='pending'
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can be None when is_sent is true, producing a sent budget with no timestamp; conversely sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some when is_sent is false, producing a phantom-sent budget
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the enum variant: `BudgetStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }` so the timestamp is only present when the budget is actually sent

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive domain identifier with no validation, newtype wrapping, or parse boundary; any caller can construct invalid IDs directly
findings.failure_mode: Callers can create BudgetWorkflow with empty string, unbounded string, or non-UUID string as the id; no smart constructor validates or rejects hostile input at the boundary
findings.fix: Introduce `BudgetId` newtype with a private inner type and a fallible smart constructor (e.g. `BudgetId::try_from(s: &str)`) that validates length/pattern on construction

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly overwrites status to 'sent' and sets is_sent=true without checking any precondition; the budget could be in any state including already sent, rejected, or never validated
findings.failure_mode: A rejected budget, an empty-budget, or a never-validated budget can all be marked as sent with zero guardrails; this is a state-machine invariant violation at runtime with no compile-time protection
findings.fix: Replace with a method on the enum typestate that matches on the current state: `fn try_mark_sent(self) -> Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetError::NotValidated>` returning an error for invalid source states

findings.problem: All fields of BudgetWorkflow are pub, allowing any caller to mutate status, booleans, and sent_at_epoch_ms directly, bypassing all smart constructors and invariants
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can write `item.status = "banana"; item.is_validated = false; item.is_sent = true;` producing a struct that violates every lifecycle invariant without the struct or module even noticing
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide smart constructors (e.g. `BudgetWorkflow::new(id)`) and state-transition methods that enforce invariants

findings.problem: mark_sent sets status='sent' and is_sent=true but never populates sent_at_epoch_ms, leaving it at whatever value it had before (likely None)
findings.failure_mode: A budget transitions to 'sent' state with no timestamp recorded, violating audit and temporal invariants; callers must manually set sent_at_epoch_ms after mark_sent, but the field is pub so they could also set it before marking
findings.fix: Have mark_sent accept or capture the timestamp: `fn mark_sent(item: BudgetWorkflow, sent_at_epoch_ms: u64) -> BudgetWorkflow` or move timestamp into the enum variant as described above

residual_risk: The struct makes illegal states fully representable at compile time. Any caller can construct a BudgetWorkflow with status="banana", is_validated=false, is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(0). The mark_sent function enforces zero preconditions. Without enum-based typestates, the state machine is enforced only by convention, not by the type system. This is a fundamental architecture violation that no amount of runtime checking can fix.
